newsitem.title: INDIA: Asian nations adopt infrastructure action plan.
newsitem.headline: Asian nations adopt infrastructure action plan.

text.p: A regional ministerial conference on infrastructure on Tuesday adopted an action plan to attract private investment and increase the pace of core projects in Asia and the Pacific.
The United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) launched the "New Delhi Action Plan" on the second and last day of the ministerial conference.

"A major outcome of the conference was the adoption of the action plan which reaffirms the commitment of countries for infrastructure development in the region," Dr Ling Liong Sik, Malaysian Minister of Transport, told a news conference.
Some 30 ESCAP member states approved the plan which emphasised the need for transparency and less red tape.
ESCAP estimates developing countries in the Asia-Pacific region need $1.5 trillion in new core sector development between 1993 and 2000, of which only $500 billion has been committed.
Investors in India, the conference's host country, complain that red tape and obscure guidelines have slowed investment in core sectors such as power, telecommunications and transport.

The plan proposes projects -- to be monitored by international and regional agencies -- for increasing the efficiency of the infrastructure sector, raising confidence in the development process and creating an environment to attract private investment.
It suggests that governments review and streamline federal administrative controls and procedures, and ensure the equitable sharing of risk between the private and public sectors.
